Telescope 5.0 is the desktop app rewritten in Rust. It starts about three times faster and needs less CPU while streaming. The phone app and the protocol are the same, so your phones keep working without pairing again.

## Faster

Measured on one Linux machine (8-core Ryzen 7 9800X3D, KDE on Wayland), streaming a 1080p30 clip at about 8 Mbps with every default plugin loaded in both apps. Medians of 4 runs, 8 for the start.

- Start to first window: 941 ms before, 297 ms now.
- CPU while streaming 1080p30: 23.2% of one core before, 17.1% now. With hardware decoding it's 17.9% before and 7.0% now.
- On disk: about 664 MB before, about 68 MB now (Python's libraries were most of that).

The window isn't any smaller in memory (about 249 MB against 226 MB), and no frames were dropped in either version. I didn't measure Windows, Background blur or Auto framing. The numbers and how they were taken are in `rust/FINDINGS.md`.

## Things to know

- **Plugins written in Python don't run any more.** They have to be rewritten in Lua (shaders in WGSL, cards in `.slint`). `docs/writing-plugins.md` has the details, and `check-plugin` checks one from the terminal and points at the line of a shader error.
- **Linux no longer needs Python.** It only needs v4l2loopback, and adb is optional. The VA-API setup button is gone because hardware decoding now finds the card itself (VA-API or CUDA on Linux, Direct3D 11 on Windows) and the line under the switch says which.
- **The first start cleans up after Python**, removing the old `lib-` folders and the leftover requirements files.
- **You can go back to the Python version (4.4.2, its last release)** in Settings, Updates, **Go back to the Python version**. It saves a dated copy of your settings first, leaves your phones alone and turns off 4.4.2's own update check so it doesn't offer Rust back. Settings and Lua plugins added since then don't carry over. The phone app has to match: uninstall the newer one first, since Android won't downgrade it, then install the 4.4.2 apk and pair again.
- On Linux going back sets up Python's libraries first, which needs the internet, Python 3.12 or newer with venv, and a few minutes. If that fails nothing is changed. An AppImage can't swap itself, so it opens the 4.4.2 page instead. I haven't tried going back on a real Windows PC.

## New

- AppImage (`Telescope-x86_64.AppImage`) for Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 36 or newer, and it doesn't need libfuse2.
- Every colour grading control can go on a keyboard shortcut, and there is an **Add phone shortcut**.
- **Reset to defaults** on the Plugins tab replaces Turn all back on. Optional plugins go off and the rest go on.
- Plugins can read the person mask in their shaders.

## Fixed

- Browser camera in Firefox now holds the resolution you picked at about the frame rate you asked for. Before, Firefox stepped down to 2 fps and stayed there.
- VHS, CRT, Desk mode and Background blur ran at 16 to 20 fps on a real stream. They hold the full frame rate at 1080p now.
- Full-range JPEG greys were crushed (16 and 235 turned into pure black and white).
- A stream's memory is handed back when it ends.
- Copy diagnostics and Restart do what they say.
- Saved virtual camera slots work again, and a browser's settings are only saved once you change something.
- Downloads retry after a timeout instead of failing.
- A failed update on Windows rolls back everything it changed.
- Settings and plugin windows stay above the main window, and Wayland windows get their icon.
- The Windows exe has its icon and name, which the tray and the firewall prompt show.

## Under the hood

Firefox reads the one frame of delay its encoder adds as overload and steps the frame rate down to 2 fps for good. Browser camera now clears that step-down and tells the browser what it may send every second.

adb doesn't set `TCP_NODELAY`. The last piece of every frame over USB waited for a 40 ms delayed ACK until Telescope started asking for the ACK straight away after each read (Linux only for now, Windows has no workaround yet, see `docs/upstream-bugs.md`).
